scope: Proposition 3.2 (Fluid realization and a pressure refinement) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix ν > 0. A finite collection of the preceding motions, repeated with period one, or preceded by one finite loading interval, yields a smooth prescribed velocity U with U(0) = 0. Suppose its spatial support is contained in one compact set in R3, or its potentials are contained in interior torus charts. Then f = Ut + (U · ∇)U − ν∆U (7) has the same support and time periodicity and bounded mixed derivatives of every order. The solution is (U, 0), with the uniqueness and material-flow conclusions of Lemma 2.2. In R3 its uniqueness statement also holds when the competing pressure has an H1 representative at each time, without requiring continuity into H1, while the other velocity hypotheses of Section 2 are retained. On the torus U and f have zero mean. Under the effective-data assumptions of Lemma 3.1, the formula is f0 + νf1 with effective coefficients; evaluation is effective for computable ν, and relative to ν otherwise.
